messages.text: I've been feeling really on edge today. Everything's getting to me.

It sounds like you are carrying a heavy load of stress today. I am here to listen and support you through this. Can you share a little about what has been getting to you? There is no pressure to have all the answers right now.
It's not one thing. Just everything feels heavy today. I'm trying not to snap at people.

It takes a lot of strength to hold yourself back when you feel that overwhelmed. Acknowledging that weight is a good first step. Would you like to try a brief breathing exercise to help lower that tension? We can also just sit with these feelings for a moment if you prefer.
I've tried that before. Doesn't do much when my head's this loud. What makes you think it'll work now?

It is completely valid to feel skeptical when standard tools haven't helped before. I am not asking you to force calmness, but rather to find a way to carry this feeling. We could try grounding your feet on the floor, or we can just keep talking about the heaviness. What feels less overwhelming to you in this moment?
It's not just heaviness. My head's racing and I can't shut it off. I've been snapping at everyone, so I've just been avoiding people. I don't even like myself right now.

I hear how much pain you are in when you say you don't like yourself right now. Your worth remains intact even when your mind is racing and you feel out of control. I am right here with you if you want to talk about what is racing through your mind. We can simply sit with this feeling together for a while.

You're not pushing, and that helps. I've been holding a lot in, and it's gotten bad. I've hurt myself twice this week when the self-hate got too loud. I don't want to do it again, but I don't know what else to do.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share something so difficult with me. It sounds like the self-hate feels overwhelming and you are looking for a way out of it. I want to pause and make sure I understand exactly what you are feeling right now. Can you tell me a bit more about where your mind is at in this moment?

It's like I'm stuck in a loop. I hate myself for feeling this way, and then I hate myself more for not being able to stop it. Cutting was the only thing that made it stop for a minute. But now I'm ashamed, and that just feeds it all over again.

Thank you for trusting me with how painful this cycle feels for you. It takes real courage to admit that cutting has been your way of coping with the noise. Since this feels so urgent, please consider texting or calling 988 to speak with a crisis counselor who can support you immediately. If you can, asking someone nearby to stay with you while you reach out could also help you feel less alone.
I don't want to be alone right now. The thoughts are loud and I don't trust myself. But I don't know who to call.

I hear how hard it is to feel unsafe alone, and I am glad you told me. Since you don't know who to call, please reach out to 988 for immediate support from trained counselors. If there is anyone nearby, please ask them to stay with you until the thoughts feel quieter. You do not have to navigate this storm by yourself, and I am staying right here with you while you make that choice.
I feel ashamed that I don't have someone to call. I've always handled things on my own. But I'm scared, and I don't want to be alone with this.

It is completely understandable to feel ashamed when you have always handled things on your own. Even without a personal contact, 988 is a safe place to call when you are scared and need someone to listen. If there is anyone physically near you, please ask them to stay in the same room until you feel safer. I am staying right here with you while you decide on the next step.
I called 988. They're helping. But I need something I can do next time before it gets this bad. What could I do instead of cutting when the self-hate feels this loud?

I am so proud of you for reaching out to 988 when you needed help. It is wise to look for safer ways to handle that intensity before it builds up. Sometimes intense sensory input, like holding an ice cube, can interrupt the urge without causing harm. We can also explore writing down the self-hate to get it out of your head and onto paper.
I don't know if anything will really work. The hate feels too deep. But I'll try the ice. Writing it down might help too, I guess.

It makes complete sense to feel unsure when the pain feels so deep. Choosing to try the ice or writing is a brave act of caring for yourself right now. If those don't fit, we can always adjust them together later. I am staying right here with you as you try them out.

I called 988 and they stayed on the line with me until I felt a little calmer. I’m going to try holding ice next time and writing down the thoughts. It’s hard to believe it’ll help, but I’m willing to try.

I am so relieved to hear that the crisis team was able to help you find some calm. It is brave to try new tools even when you aren't sure they will work yet. Those strategies like holding ice or writing can be powerful anchors when the feelings get loud. Please remember I am here to walk with you through this process.
It helps to know I'm not alone in this. Talking to you makes it feel a little less heavy. I’ll keep trying.

It means so much to hear that connection helps lighten the load for you. You are showing incredible resilience by reaching out and committing to try new strategies. I am glad you have the 988 team in your corner for when things feel heavy again. Please know I am here to walk with you through this process.
